The cloak is composed of identical nanosized chalcogenide glass resonators made of GeSbSe glass with dielectric constant 10.5–12 at 1–1.5 µm wavelength.
Resonators are cylindrical with diameters of 300 nm and heights of 150 nm.
Resonators are arranged in concentric cylindrical arrays along radial spokes to optimize magnetic dipole orientation.
Air fractions between resonators are varied radially to achieve the required spatial distribution of effective permeability.
The effective permeability in the cloak ranges from 0 at the inner radius to 1 at the outer radius.
Resonance halos extend beyond the physical resonator volume, influencing inter-resonator spacing and coupling.
The maximum packing density avoids halo overlap by maintaining inter-resonator distances of at least three times the halo volume.
Full-wave simulations show wavefront reconstruction after passing the cloak, confirming cloaking effectiveness.
The cloak hides a metal cylinder of 15 µm diameter using a cloak shell thickness of 4 µm.
The cloak operates near 300 THz (infrared range) with a bandwidth of 3.5 THz (1.2%), potentially extendable to 8 THz (2.8%).
Fabrication feasibility was demonstrated by producing glass grating structures with 300 nm wide mesas and 150 nm height using e-beam lithography.
The cloak design is based on transformation optics principles for cylindrical objects.
Simulations applied periodic boundary conditions to model an infinitely long cylindrical cloak.
The effective permittivity in the design was about 1.2, slightly less than the ideal 2.7, but this did not significantly affect performance.
The cloak's magnetic resonance modes are excited over a wide frequency range, unlike some previous designs limited to single frequencies.
The number of resonators in the first layer can be about 60 for a cloak inner radius of 6.5 µm.
The cloak uses nonmetallic dielectric resonators, reducing losses compared to metal-based metamaterials.
The cloak's design accounts for discrete resonator responses, including shape and inter-resonator coupling.
The radial growth of air fraction does not follow the square law prescribed by classical transformation optics but is adjusted to fit resonance halo effects.
The cloak was simulated to conceal objects ranging from five to ten wavelengths in size.
